content:
marta: Quick heads-up — perf regression in multi-GPU e2e for lp-serve after the kernel-selector change. 99th latency up ~18% on 8-GPU p4d runs.

sam: saw that in CI too. trace attached in the job, looks like all-reduce tails.

jin: can you paste the tracepoint where it spikes? is it after kv-cache hits or during forward chunking?

marta: pasted snippet from perf trace: 
```
[0.00s] compute kernel A (batch 32)
[0.12s] nccl allreduce start (small msgs)
[0.18s] host sync waiting on stream 3
[0.26s] compute kernel B delayed
[... tail spikes at 0.18s - 0.35s]
```

kai: interesting — sounds like channel contention. we've been defaulting to single channel for LL128 in this config. that can cause head-of-line blocking when small messages interleave with medium ones.

sam: i instrumented NCCL counters: queue depth saturates at ~64 for channel 0, other channels idle. NVLink bw_util shows uneven usage.

jin: hypothesis: kernel selector switched some layers to fused kernels that produce more frequent small allreduces (grad syncs), increasing interleaving. combined with single-channel LL128 -> queuing.

marta: agree. quick experiment plan: 1) run with NCCL_PROTO=LL, NCCL_ALGO=Ring to compare 2) try NCCL_MAX_NRINGS=4 / NCCL_NTHREADS tweaking 3) enable per-stream channel mapping (ncclChannelsPerProxy?) and pin heavy layers to dedicated channels.

sam: also try NCCL_LL_THRESHOLD=0 to force LL path and compare. and set NCCL_COLLNET_ENABLE=0 to remove collnet noise.

kai: i can spin up 3 jobs. i'll run these env variations: 
- baseline (current kernel selector build)
- NCCL_PROTO=LL128 NCCL_ALGO=Tree NCCL_MAX_NRINGS=2
- NCCL_PROTO=LL NCCL_ALGO=Ring NCCL_MAX_NRINGS=4
- per-stream affinity: export NCCL_LAUNCH_MODE=PARALLEL + pin streams in runtime map

jin: also toggle our batching heuristic: reduce max_batch_latency from 12ms -> 6ms so compute dispatches more frequently (might reduce bursty small messages).

marta: good call. include kv-cache warmup toggles too (prepopulate KV for first few steps) to see if early misses amplify contention.

tracebot: perf trace uploaded -> https://internal/traces/2240123456/trace.json : shows per-channel occupancy and stream waits.

sam: initial run results (quick summary): 
- baseline: 99p +18%
- LL, Ring, MAX_NRINGS=4: 99p -7% vs baseline (better)
- LL128, Tree, MAX_NRINGS=2: 99p +4%
- affinity + reduced batching latency: 99p -12% (best so far)

kai: nice. so forcing LL (non-LL128) + more rings helped, and stream/channel affinity + batching tweak best. suggests LL128 with single channel was the bad combo.

marta: action items: 
- jin: add per-layer channel hints in kernel selector config (opt-in flag) and expose runtime knob to map heavy allreduces to separate channels (due by EOD).
- sam: create perf dashboard widget for per-channel queue depth and 99p breakdown (tomorrow).
- kai: schedule a broader sweep across p3/p4 families to ensure changes generalize (this week).

jin: quick note — need to guard per-layer hints behind feature flag; we might cause imbalance on smaller rigs. will add safe defaults.

sam: also add a test in our perf harness that runs with varying NCCL_PROTO/algo combos and asserts 99p within X% of baseline.

marta: thanks all. if anyone sees regression after the per-layer channel hint PR, ping #eng-runtime on the PR and i'll triage. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: canary cluster redeployed with kernel-selector revert for affected tag.

kai: leaving logs here for reference: /mnt/artifacts/2240123456/nccl-channel-sweep/ (contains env, runs, traces)

marta: perfect — i'll draft a short postmortem in #postmortems if the change ships, but this looks like an operational tuning issue rather than a correctness bug.

sam: one more: add a note in docs about LL128 requiring careful channel config for mixed-message workloads. short blurb in internal runbooks.

jin: PR incoming for channel hints + config. linking in thread when ready.

marta: thanks — will review.
